title: Price slate & hiring convergence scenario — April 2027
content:
Executive summary:
- Purpose: rapid scenario workbook to assess how small price slate changes (per-token and slab options) interact with planned hiring over next 4 quarters. Goal is a decision signal: if price draft A/B recommended, what hiring freeze / defer actions are near-term needed to protect margin targets.

High-level conclusions (quick):
1) A +6% per-token increase against current base drives margin improvement but triggers ~10% churn risk on mid-market trials. Net effect on ARR in Q3 is neutral unless we pair with a lower slab entry price.
2) If we keep customer-facing slabs constant and raise per-token by >8%, we can avoid hiring 6 junior infra hires planned for Q3 but should accelerate 2 SRE hires to protect latency SLA.
3) The least-regret move: staggered price-slate rollout (small per-token + slab entry discount for annual prepay) preserves GTM velocity while giving ops 8 weeks to evaluate capacity.

Key inputs / assumptions (short):
- Baseline monthly token volume (all customers): 45B tokens
- Baseline blended per-token revenue: $0.0009/token
- Slab entry price (starter): $250/month for 100k tokens equivalent
- Variable cost per token (inference + infra amort): $0.00045/token (weighted avg across hosted/dedicated mix)
- Planned hires (Q2–Q4 2027): 8 total (3 infra, 2 SRE, 2 sales SDR, 1 finance analyst)
- Churn sensitivity: assumed elasticity: d(churn)/d(price) = 0.012 per % increase for SMB, 0.006 for mid-market, 0.002 for enterprise (weighted customers -> effective 0.0075)
- ARR conversion delay: price changes impact booked ARR with a 6–12 week lag (sales cycles)

Scenario matrix (abbreviated):
Columns: scenario_id | per-token delta (%) | slab entry delta (%) | demand elasticity adj | est monthly margin delta ($k) | headcount action recommendation | risk notes
- S1 | +2% | 0% | -0.015 | +120 | no hires deferred | low risk
- S2 | +6% | 0% | -0.045 | +360 | defer 3 junior infra hires to Q4 | moderate (trial friction)
- S3 | +8% | -10% slab | -0.02 | +280 | keep hires, re-sequence (move 2 infra -> SRE) | lower churn, needs GTM coordination
- S4 | +12% | 0% | -0.09 | +720 | freeze all non-critical hiring (except SLA protectors) | high churn risk for SMB

Simplified headcount cost table (plan vs option):
- Role, FTEs planned, avg fully-burdened cost / mo, planned start quarter
- Infra eng (junior), 3, $18,000, Q3 2027
- SRE (mid), 2, $28,000, Q3 2027
- Sales SDR, 2, $12,000, Q4 2027
- Finance analyst, 1, $14,000, Q3 2027
Total monthly payroll impact if hires added in Q3 = $ (3*18k + 2*28k + 2*12k + 14k) = $ (54k + 56k + 24k + 14k) = $148k/mo -> $1.776M annualized

Decision heuristics (working):
- If scenario incremental margin improvement < 2x monthly payroll increment for new hires -> delay hires.
- If projected churn uplift > 3% on average -> require stepped rollouts + trial cohort protections.
- If latency incidents predicted to exceed 99.9 SLA risk window under demand model -> prioritize SRE hires even if headcount freeze elsewhere.

Simple calculation examples (cells):
- incremental_revenue = baseline_tokens * per_token_delta
- incremental_margin = incremental_revenue - baseline_tokens * variable_cost_delta
- payroll_savings_if_defer = sum(fb_costs of deferred roles)
Example numeric (S2):
- baseline_tokens = 45,000,000,000 tokens/mo -> 45B
- per_token_delta = +6% on $0.0009 -> new price = 0.000954 -> delta 0.000054
- incremental_revenue = 45B * 0.000054 = $2,430,000/mo
- incremental_variable_cost (if cost per token stays same) = 45B * 0.00045 * 0 = 0 (we assume cost unchanged per token)
- BUT apply demand elasticity -> demand drop = 4.5% -> effective tokens = 42.975B -> net incremental_revenue = 42.975B * 0.000054 = $2,320,650/mo
- incremental_margin approx = $2.32M/mo year -> significant vs monthly payroll $148k -> suggests hires could be deferred and still net positive.

Open items / TODOs: 
- Validate elasticity assumptions with Growth (tag: @Maya Singh) — last churn study was May 2026 and used different SKU mixes.
- Model effect of tiered slab re-pricing (starter discount + per-token bump) on conversion velocity (need SDR funnel conversion delta).
- Add latency-cost sensitivity: run micro-sim of 95th percentile inference cost if usage drops by 5% but spike events persist.
- Coordinate with Legal on comms cadence for price changes (contract language for annual prepay).

Notes for ops:
- If we intend to defer 3 infra hires, reassign one senior infra to mentor and temporarily hold backlog for non-critical features.
- Consider hiring 1 contract SRE for 12 weeks as hedge if we want to avoid permanent hires but close SLA risk window. Cost tradeoff: contract SRE ~ $40k/mo vs 2 full-time SREs $56k/mo.

Appendix: quick sensitivity grid (monthly net margin delta vs price change and demand elasticity):
- columns: price_delta_pct [0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12], rows: effective_demand_elasticity [-0.002, -0.005, -0.01, -0.02, -0.04]
- populate by formula described above (spreadsheet tab pending)

Slack links / context:
- #fin-pricing (thread id: ts-346) — early commentary from GTM about customer sensitivity
- Growth retrospective: confluence:GRW-CHURN-2026 (elasticity inference notes)

Quick ask to leadership:
- Approve runway to defer up to $300k/month of hiring spend if we choose S2/S4 path, with caveat that we keep 2 SRE hires on schedule.
- Authorize fast A/B of price-slate for 8% cohort (select 5 large trials) for 10 weeks to measure real churn signal before org-wide rollout.
